messages:
zoe_sales: Quick escalation  HelioWorks POC: demo operator reports ~30% of exported Splunk rows have empty trace_id column; Console shows traces for most requests but some requests don't link. They also hit spikes of 429s during a bulk import. Can we swarm? :boom:

lucas_se: on it. Can you paste one redacted request + the forwarder log line? Need to know whether the header reaches our gateway and where it gets lost.

zoe_sales: pasted from ticket (redacted):
```
POST /v1/complete 200 OK
Headers: { Authorization: Bearer REDACTED, X-Trace-Id: helio-9a, traceparent: 00-helio9a000000000000000000000000-01 }
Client log:
[2026-05-02T10:12:03Z] WARN status=429 id=req-998 trace=helio-9a
[2026-05-02T10:12:04Z] INFO forwarder.hec send status=ok trace=
```

lucas_se: hmmm. I noticed a cluster of customers using an older Splunk forwarder that sends batched payloads with gzip chunking; some of those forwarders rewrite or omit lightly-populated headers on inner batch items. Two plausible roots: (A) our export worker only copies trace headers when present on the top-level HTTP envelope (not per-batch item), or (B) the customer's forwarder is dropping headers inside the gzip/batch.

ena_sre: quick plan: (1) scan export logs for events missing metadata.trace_id for org=helio, (2) check the Splunk drain connector config for 'batch_mode' and 'preserve_headers' flags, (3) temporarily raise POC token QPS so they don't hit 429s during the demo. Need approval for a short window.

zoe_sales: I can approve a 20-minute bump for the demo. Demo starts in 35 minutes.

ena_sre: done  raised token_qps to 8rps for org=helio for 20m and turned on debug export logging.

deploy-bot: runtime change scheduled: poc-token-qps-bump -> org-helio (owner: ena_sre). Canary: 5% traffic.

deploy-bot: canary OK. change rolled to 100% for org-helio.

lucas_se: mitigation I can push: exporter will now extract trace id from three places per incoming item (priority order): event.metadata.trace_id || batch-item.headers.X-Trace-Id || batch-item.headers.traceparent (extract). It will then inject metadata.trace_id on every exported event before batching/compression. Deploying small canary now.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started: exporter-batch-trace-fix v0.7.0 -> p-prod-canary (owner: lucas_se)

deploy-bot: canary health: 10/10 checks passed, 2% traffic routed.

lucas_se: verified on canary: exported events now include metadata.trace_id=helio-9a in batch items; Splunk HEC rows show matching ids. Missing-rate dropped from ~30% -> ~3% in canary slice.

zoe_sales: great. Anything I should send to HelioWorks ops immediately?

ena_sre: short runbook for customer ops:
1) If you use an intermediate forwarder that batches/gzips events, enable per-item header preservation or add the trace id into each event's metadata (key `metadata.trace_id`) before batching.
2) When creating the Splunk HEC drain, set `map_trace_id=metadata.trace_id`. Example: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/drains \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <org-token>" \
  -d '{"type":"splunk_hec","url":"https://splunk.helio:8088/services/collector","token":"HEC_TOKEN","map_trace_id":"metadata.trace_id","preserve_headers":true}'
```
3) For short demos, request `trace_sampling: full` or ask us for a temporary `token_qps` bump to avoid 429s. `trace_sampling: full` increases export volume.

lucas_se: FYI the long-term fix we prefer on our side is `exporter.attach_trace_context=true` which will unconditionally annotate every export item with an extracted trace id when present on the HTTP context or incoming payload. We can gate that behind a config per-org if they prefer.

mark_security: security checklist: confirm HEC endpoint uses TLS and that the HEC token scope is ingest-only. Also capture the customer's written approval for the 20-minute QPS bump; I'll add that entry to the security approvals log for this POC.

zoe_sales: HelioWorks confirmed TLS + ingest-only HEC token and approved the 20m QPS bump. I'm scheduling a quick ops pairing call to walk through header preservation and the drain config. Thanks all  super helpful. :raised_hands:
